```{r Question 1-3}



fpath<-file.path("C:","Users","tdthe","Downloads","breast+cancer+wisconsin+original", .Platform$file.sep)
dataset_name<-paste(fpath, "breast-cancer-wisconsin.data", sep="")
names_name<-paste(fpath, "breast-cancer-wisconsin.names", sep="")
data_names<-c("Sample code number", "Clump Thickness", "Uniformity of Cell Size", "Uniformity of Cell Shape", "Marginal Adhesion", "Single Epithelial Cell Size", "Bare Nuclei", "Bland Chromatin", "Normal Nucleoli", "Mitoses", "Class")
dataset<-read.csv(dataset_name, col.names = data_names)

#Dataset without missing values
updated_dataset <- dataset[-grep("?", dataset$Bare.Nuclei, fixed=TRUE), ]

#To change Bare.Nuclei from chr to int
updated_dataset$Bare.Nuclei<-as.integer(updated_dataset$Bare.Nuclei)

#This is to check which ones are Benign and which one is Malignant
bein_data<-which(updated_dataset$Class=="2")
mal_data<-which(updated_dataset$Class=="4")

#Since Malignant tumors are less common, we will under sample ?benign? tumors to adjust for imbalance for the dataset
#To ensure consistency
set.seed(1234)
nsamp<-length(mal_data)
pick_bein<-sample(bein_data, nsamp)


balanced_data<-as.data.frame(updated_dataset[c(pick_bein,mal_data),])

cancer_PC<-prcomp(balanced_data, scale.=TRUE) #the scaled PCA 
summary(cancer_PC)
```
Looking at this, PC6 have 89.625% cumulative proportion of variance and PC7 have 92.646% cumulative proportion of variance, so we will use the first 7 Principal Components to classify the data. 

```{r KNN}
library(class)
library(ggplot2)


pca_data<-as.data.frame(cancer_PC$x[, 1:7]) #the data frame of the PCA from 1 to 7 (which is the 90% variablity)
classes<-balanced_data$Class #The 2 classes, benign or malignant

set.seed(1234) #to ensure consistency
size<-floor(0.8*nrow(pca_data)) #382 observations in the training sample while 96 in the testing sample

#splitting the data into a testing and training sample
train_sample<-sample(seq_len(nrow(pca_data)),size=size)
#training data
cancer_train<-pca_data[train_sample,]
train_class<-classes[train_sample]
#testing data
cancer_test<-pca_data[-train_sample,]
test_class<-classes[-train_sample]

#K-NN with the training sample as train, testing sample as test, the classes as cl, and k=19 (high enough compared to the training sample)
cancer_knn <- knn(train = cancer_train, test = cancer_test, cl=train_class, k = 19)
#This will show how much K-NN predicted in benign (2) or malignant (4)
summary(cancer_knn)

#This is to help visualize the predicted K-NN with respect to the PCs
knn_complete<-data.frame(PC1=cancer_test$PC1,
                            PC2=cancer_test$PC2,
                            PC3=cancer_test$PC3,
                            PC4=cancer_test$PC4,
                            PC5=cancer_test$PC5,
                            PC6=cancer_test$PC6,
                            PC7=cancer_test$PC7,
                            knn=cancer_knn)

#As examples to visualize the K-NN predication

ggplot(knn_complete, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = knn, fill=knn)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(title = "2D PCA Visualization (PC1 vs PC2) with K-NN",
       x = "Principal Component 1", y = "Principal Component 2", color = "K-NN Label") +
  theme_minimal()


```
